boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Seattle University
boards.description: Ten currently documented late-opening food destinations in and around Capitol Hill and First Hill, selected for under-21-safe visits.

cards.title: Lost Lake Cafe
cards.subtitle: 1505 10th Ave, Capitol Hill
cards.notes: Check the day before heading out: the cafe lists midnight closes Sunday–Wednesday, 2 a.m. Thursday, and 3 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.short_summary: A Capitol Hill cafe with the latest listed closing time in this set on Fridays and Saturdays.
cards.evidence_claim: Lost Lake Cafe lists hours of 7 a.m.–midnight Sunday–Wednesday, 7 a.m.–2 a.m. Thursday, and 7 a.m.–3 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Current official hours: Sun–Wed 7 a.m.–midnight; Thu 7 a.m.–2 a.m.; Fri–Sat 7 a.m.–3 a.m. Reconfirm before travel.

cards.title: Dick's Drive-In Broadway
cards.subtitle: 115 Broadway E, Capitol Hill
cards.notes: Use the Broadway location page before leaving; it lists daily service through 2 a.m. and identifies this as the Capitol Hill location.
cards.short_summary: A clearly identified Capitol Hill drive-in with the same late closing time every day.
cards.evidence_claim: Dick's Drive-In's Broadway location is listed as open daily from 10:30 a.m. to 2 a.m.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists daily hours of 10:30 a.m.–2 a.m.; verify holiday changes before going.

cards.title: Big Mario's Capitol Hill
cards.subtitle: 1009 E Pike St, Capitol Hill
cards.notes: Plan around the published schedule: weekday service starts at 11 a.m., weekends at noon, and the Capitol Hill shop lists a 2 a.m. close.
cards.short_summary: A named Capitol Hill pizza location with daily late hours and a later Friday–Saturday slice window.
cards.evidence_claim: Big Mario's lists its Capitol Hill location as open until 2 a.m. daily, with a Friday–Saturday slice window until 3 a.m.
cards.source_title: Big Mario's New York Style Pizza
cards.access_notes: Official site lists Capitol Hill open until 2 a.m. daily; Friday–Saturday slice window is listed 2–3 a.m. Check holiday notices.

cards.title: Olympia Pizza & Spaghetti House 3
cards.subtitle: 212 Broadway E, Capitol Hill
cards.notes: Confirm the kitchen timing if ordering food late: the restaurant lists daily operation until 2 a.m., with the kitchen serving until 1 a.m.
cards.short_summary: A Capitol Hill pizza-and-pasta restaurant whose official page distinguishes its kitchen closing time.
cards.evidence_claim: Olympia Pizza & Spaghetti House 3 lists daily hours of 11 a.m.–2 a.m. and kitchen hours of 11 a.m.–1 a.m.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists the business open daily 11 a.m.–2 a.m.; kitchen listed until 1 a.m. Arrive before kitchen close for food.

cards.title: Pie Bar Capitol Hill
cards.subtitle: 1361 E Olive Way, Capitol Hill
cards.notes: Visit on an operating night and check the site’s closure notices; it lists Tuesday–Thursday 8 p.m.–2 a.m. and Friday–Sunday 5 p.m.–2 a.m.
cards.short_summary: A Capitol Hill pie destination with a late-evening opening schedule rather than daytime service.
cards.evidence_claim: Pie Bar Capitol Hill lists hours until 2 a.m. Tuesday through Sunday, opening at 8 p.m. Tuesday–Thursday and 5 p.m. Friday–Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists 2 a.m. closes Tuesday–Sunday and notes periodic closures; confirm the date before visiting.

cards.title: Momiji
cards.subtitle: 1522 12th Ave, Capitol Hill
cards.notes: Use this for a late dinner on Friday or Saturday: the restaurant’s posted kitchen schedule runs until midnight on those two nights.
cards.short_summary: A 12th Avenue Japanese restaurant with documented midnight weekend kitchen hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Momiji lists kitchen hours of 4 p.m.–midnight Friday and Saturday, and 4–11 p.m. Sunday through Thursday.
cards.access_notes: Official posted kitchen hours reach midnight Friday–Saturday. Confirm reservations and holiday service directly with the restaurant.

cards.title: DeLuxe Bar & Grill
cards.subtitle: 625 Broadway E, Capitol Hill
cards.notes: Check the day-specific schedule before walking over; the restaurant lists Friday and Saturday closing at midnight, later than its weekday service.
cards.short_summary: A longstanding Broadway restaurant with documented midnight Friday and Saturday hours.
cards.evidence_claim: DeLuxe Bar & Grill lists Friday hours of noon–midnight and Saturday hours of 10 a.m.–midnight.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists midnight closing on Friday and Saturday; check the live site for temporary schedule changes.

cards.title: IHOP on East Madison
cards.subtitle: 950 E Madison St, First Hill
cards.notes: Keep the official location page handy for the address and dine-in status; it lists this Seattle restaurant as open 24 hours every day.
cards.short_summary: A First Hill pancake restaurant with official 24-hour daily operation listed.
cards.evidence_claim: IHOP's official Seattle location page lists the restaurant at 950 E Madison St as open 24 hours Monday through Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists 24-hour service every day and identifies dine-in as an amenity. Verify exceptional holiday hours before travel.

cards.title: Chick'N'Crunch Capitol Hill
cards.subtitle: 1525 13th Ave, Capitol Hill
cards.notes: Treat the posted weekend hours as delivery availability and confirm the ordering platform before relying on it; the site lists Saturday and Sunday service until 2 a.m.
cards.short_summary: A 13th Avenue halal chicken-bowl location with published weekend late-night service.
cards.evidence_claim: Chick'N'Crunch states that its Capitol Hill location has weekend late-night service from midnight to 2 a.m. Saturday and Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Official site describes Saturday–Sunday 12–2 a.m. late-night service and links delivery platforms; confirm fulfillment availability before ordering.

cards.title: Dino's Tomato Pie
cards.subtitle: 1524 E Olive Way, Capitol Hill
cards.notes: Plan a Thursday–Saturday food run and recheck the restaurant’s live channels before departure; current local reporting lists a 2 a.m. close those nights.
cards.short_summary: An East Olive Way pizzeria reported to keep later weekend-adjacent hours than its early-week schedule.
cards.evidence_claim: A July 2026 Seattle dining guide reports Dino's Tomato Pie open until midnight Sunday–Wednesday and until 2 a.m. Thursday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: The Best Late-Night Restaurants in Seattle — The Infatuation
cards.access_notes: Current local reporting lists Thursday–Saturday service until 2 a.m.; reconfirm directly with the restaurant for same-night or holiday hours.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Seattle University spaces for studying, creating, gathering, recreation, and reflection, each supported by a current university source.

cards.title: Lemieux Library
cards.subtitle: Library and learning commons near the Student Center
cards.notes: Use the library for a solo work session, group project, research help, or a meet-up; its official page identifies all four as supported uses.
cards.short_summary: A central academic hub with study, technology, and research support.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University describes Lemieux Library as a space for studying, group work, creative projects, and meeting friends, with resources, services, and technology.
cards.access_notes: SU ID is required for building access during Summer Quarter and Intersession; check the library page for detailed hours.

cards.title: Garden Reading Room
cards.subtitle: First floor, Lemieux Library
cards.notes: Bring a laptop or reading and use this named 24/7 study option when you need a library-based workspace outside regular desk hours.
cards.short_summary: A named first-floor reading room available among the library's 24/7 study spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University's new-student guide lists the Garden Reading Room on Lemieux Library's first floor as a 24/7 study space.
cards.access_notes: After-hours access to 24/7 spaces is limited to current students, staff, and faculty with an active SU ID card.

cards.title: Bangasser Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Room 214, second floor of Lemieux Library
cards.notes: Choose this named reading room for an on-campus study block, and keep an active SU ID handy if you plan to use the 24/7 spaces after hours.
cards.short_summary: A second-floor reading room included in the library's 24/7 study-space list.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University's new-student guide lists the Byte Café and Bangasser Reading Room, Room 214, among Lemieux Library's 24/7 study spaces.
cards.access_notes: After-hours access to 24/7 spaces is limited to current students, staff, and faculty with an active SU ID card.

cards.title: Billodue Makerspace
cards.subtitle: Seattle University library makerspace
cards.notes: Plan a creative project, repair session, or first-time making activity here; the library says the space supports digital and physical fabrication work.
cards.short_summary: A campus makerspace for hands-on, inclusive creative work.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University says the Billodue Makerspace is open to all students and majors and supports activities including fiber arts, jewelry making, repair sessions, laser cutting, and 3D printing.
cards.access_notes: Check the library's makerspace information for available equipment, programs, and access details.

cards.title: Media Production Center
cards.subtitle: Lemieux Library and McGoldrick Learning Commons
cards.notes: Use the studio and editing resources to develop a class or club media project, then check current program information before relying on specific equipment.
cards.short_summary: A library production space for video, photo, audio, animation, and screening projects.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University says the Media Production Center is available to all students and offers studio and editing equipment, with programs for video, photography, audio, animation, and more.
cards.access_notes: Availability of studios, editing rooms, and programs may vary; consult the library makerspace information before visiting.

cards.title: Student Center 210
cards.subtitle: Second floor of the Student Center
cards.notes: For a planned small gathering or project meeting, ask University Events about this equipped second-floor room rather than assuming it is open for drop-in use.
cards.short_summary: A named Student Center meeting and gathering room with presentation equipment.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University identifies Student Center 210 as a second-floor space for break-out sessions, meetings, and gatherings, equipped with a computer, screen, projector, and in-house sound system.
cards.access_notes: This is an event space; confirm reservation or access requirements with University Events.

cards.title: Casey Commons
cards.subtitle: Fifth floor of Casey Building
cards.notes: Consider this named commons for a medium-sized meeting or training, and coordinate with University Events if your group needs the adjacent conference rooms or atrium.
cards.short_summary: A fifth-floor Casey Building commons configured for meetings, trainings, and banquets.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University describes Casey Commons as a fifth-floor Casey Building space for medium-sized banquets, meetings, and trainings near conference rooms and the Casey Atrium.
cards.access_notes: This is an event space; confirm reservation or access requirements with University Events.

cards.title: Chapel of St. Ignatius
cards.subtitle: Seattle University's main chapel
cards.notes: Visit during posted building hours for quiet reflection, or consult the chapel calendar if you want to attend a scheduled liturgy or campus spiritual event.
cards.short_summary: A campus chapel with scheduled liturgies and a documented colored-light architectural design.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University identifies the Chapel of St. Ignatius as its main chapel, primarily hosting Roman Catholic liturgies, and invites visitors to explore its offerings and pray during the academic year.
cards.source_title: Chapel of St. Ignatius | Seattle University
cards.access_notes: Posted building hours are Monday-Friday 8 a.m.-4:30 p.m.; Saturday is closed except for scheduled events, and Sunday access is around Masses.

cards.title: Redhawk Center
cards.subtitle: 14th Avenue and East Cherry Street recreation complex
cards.notes: Bring your valid SU or UREC ID for a recreation visit, then use the pools, courts, functional-training space, or racquetball courts according to facility rules.
cards.short_summary: A named recreation facility with aquatic, court, and training spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University lists the Redhawk Center's East and West pools, North Court, Redhawk Activity Court, racquetball courts, Studio 3, and saunas among its recreation features.
cards.access_notes: Membership is restricted to eligible Seattle University community members; valid SU or UREC ID is required, and guests need a purchased pass with a current member.

cards.title: Esports Center
cards.subtitle: Student Center 330
cards.notes: Look for current UREC access or reservation guidance before setting up a gaming session; the university lists this named center as one of its recreation facilities.
cards.short_summary: A named Student Center recreation destination for esports activity.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University lists the Esports Center, located in Student Center 330, among its external recreation facilities.
cards.access_notes: Check UREC for current access and reservation details; UREC facility membership is limited to eligible Seattle University community members.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-admission ways to spend time together on campus and around Seattle, using publicly documented free access.

cards.title: Browse the Hedreen Gallery
cards.subtitle: Lee Center for the Arts, Seattle University
cards.notes: Meet at the Lee Center, take in the current exhibition together, and use the posted Wednesday–Saturday hours before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A campus gallery that is always free and open to the public.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University states that Hedreen Gallery is always free and open to the public; it is in the Lee Center for the Arts and is open Wednesday–Saturday, 1–6 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Open Wednesday–Saturday, 1–6 p.m.; the university identifies it as free and open to the public.

cards.title: Pause in the Chapel of St. Ignatius
cards.subtitle: Seattle University campus
cards.notes: Use weekday building hours for a quiet visit, or attend a listed liturgy with friends; check the chapel calendar for closures first.
cards.short_summary: Seattle U’s main chapel offers a calm shared stop during its public building hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University lists Chapel of St. Ignatius building hours as Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–4:30 p.m., and posts its Mass schedule.
cards.source_title: Chapel of St. Ignatius | Seattle University
cards.access_notes: Building hours are Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–4:30 p.m.; Sunday access is immediately before and after Mass. Check the calendar for changes.

cards.title: See art at the Frye
cards.subtitle: 704 Terry Avenue, First Hill
cards.notes: Walk over to First Hill, choose a few works to discuss, and plan around museum hours rather than a paid program or ticketed concert.
cards.short_summary: A nearby museum whose general admission is always free.
cards.evidence_claim: The Frye Art Museum states that admission is always free.
cards.access_notes: General museum admission is always free. Some separately programmed events can have registration or fees, so use the regular galleries.

cards.entity_name: Free First Thursday: Seattle Art Museum
cards.title: Do Free First Thursday at SAM
cards.subtitle: Seattle Art Museum, 1300 First Avenue
cards.notes: Put the first Thursday on the calendar, enter during the free window, and wander the galleries or join the included drop-in activities.
cards.short_summary: The downtown Seattle Art Museum has free admission on each first Thursday.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle Art Museum says admission to its downtown museum is free on the first Thursday of every month, with galleries open 10 a.m.–8 p.m.
cards.source_title: Free First Thursday | Seattle Art Museum
cards.access_notes: Free only on the first Thursday of each month; Seattle Art Museum is listed as open 10 a.m.–8 p.m. that day.

cards.entity_name: Free First Thursday: Seattle Asian Art Museum
cards.title: Visit the Asian Art Museum on First Thursday
cards.subtitle: Seattle Asian Art Museum, Volunteer Park
cards.notes: Make a first-Thursday plan around Volunteer Park, then use the free museum hours for an art-focused afternoon with your group.
cards.short_summary: The Seattle Asian Art Museum waives admission on the first Thursday each month.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle Art Museum states that Seattle Asian Art Museum admission is free on the first Thursday of every month, with hours of 10 a.m.–5 p.m.
cards.source_title: Free First Thursday | Seattle Art Museum
cards.access_notes: Free only on the first Thursday of each month; the Seattle Asian Art Museum is listed as open 10 a.m.–5 p.m.

cards.entity_name: ARTS at King Street Station Gallery
cards.title: See ARTS at King Street Station
cards.subtitle: 303 S. Jackson Street, top floor
cards.notes: Take the elevator to the top floor, view the current work at your own pace, and use Thursday evening hours when they fit the group.
cards.short_summary: A city-run gallery with regular free public hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle’s Office of Arts & Culture states that ARTS at King Street Station is free and open Wednesday–Saturday, 11 a.m.–5 p.m., with Thursday hours until 8 p.m. in 2026.
cards.source_title: ARTS at King Street Station Gallery | City of Seattle
cards.access_notes: Free Wednesday–Saturday, 11 a.m.–5 p.m.; open until 8 p.m. Thursdays in 2026. The building has an ADA-compliant elevator.

cards.entity_name: Pioneer Square First Thursday Art Walk
cards.title: Walk Pioneer Square’s First Thursday Art Walk
cards.subtitle: Pioneer Square, first Thursday of each month
cards.notes: Start at King Street Station, pick a few participating arts stops, and treat the evening as a walk-and-talk rather than a shopping outing.
cards.short_summary: A recurring neighborhood art-walk format the city describes as free.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Seattle says monthly art walks offer a free opportunity to enjoy the arts and identifies Pioneer Square’s First Thursday Art Walk as a recurring event.
cards.source_title: Art Walks | City of Seattle Office of Arts & Culture
cards.access_notes: Held on the first Thursday of the month. Individual participating businesses organize their own offerings, so confirm stops before going.

cards.title: Tour the Central Library together
cards.subtitle: Central Library, 1000 Fourth Avenue
cards.notes: Grab the self-guided tour materials, choose a route through the building’s public levels, and stop to compare favorite art or architecture details.
cards.short_summary: A self-paced architecture and art tour inside Seattle’s flagship public library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Seattle Public Library provides self-guided tour maps and an audio tour for the Central Library, and says everyone is welcome at its library locations.
cards.source_title: Take a Tour of the Central Library | The Seattle Public Library
cards.access_notes: Use the self-guided maps or audio tour during open library hours. Library system policy says everyone is welcome at its locations.

cards.title: Meet up at Capitol Hill Branch
cards.subtitle: Seattle Public Library, Capitol Hill
cards.notes: Choose a public seating area, browse together, or use the branch as a no-purchase regroup point before continuing through the neighborhood.
cards.short_summary: A public-library meet-up spot where no library card is needed simply to enter.
cards.evidence_claim: The Seattle Public Library says everyone is welcome at its library locations, including people without a library card, and lists Capitol Hill Branch among its locations.
cards.source_title: Get Started with a Library Card | The Seattle Public Library
cards.access_notes: Everyone is welcome at Seattle Public Library locations; a card is not required to enter and use many services. Check current branch hours before visiting.

cards.title: See the Soul Pole at Douglass-Truth
cards.subtitle: Douglass-Truth Branch, Seattle Public Library
cards.notes: Meet on the branch lawn to look closely at the 21-foot sculpture, then go inside to explore the branch’s public art and collection displays.
cards.short_summary: A documented community artwork at a public library branch in the Central District.
cards.evidence_claim: The Seattle Public Library identifies the Soul Pole on the Douglass-Truth Branch lawn as a 21-foot wooden sculpture depicting African American history, and says everyone is welcome at its library locations.
cards.source_title: Douglass-Truth Branch Art | The Seattle Public Library
cards.access_notes: The Soul Pole is on the branch lawn. Enter the library during posted branch hours; Seattle Public Library says everyone is welcome at its locations.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented Seattle University environments for focused work, collaborative projects, creative production, and identity-centered study time.

cards.title: Lemieux Library
cards.subtitle: Lemieux Library & McGoldrick Learning Commons
cards.notes: Set up near the center of campus for reading or project work; use the connected Student Center walkway when planning your route.
cards.short_summary: A light-filled campus library supporting individual study, group work, and creative projects.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University describes Lemieux Library as a space for studying, group work, and creative projects, with modern lab spaces.
cards.access_notes: An SU ID card is required for building access during Summer Quarter and Intersession.

cards.title: Billodue Makerspace
cards.subtitle: Sinegal Center
cards.notes: Bring a project idea and use the space’s fabrication tools or join a listed making activity to turn course concepts into physical work.
cards.short_summary: A hands-on learning space for digital fabrication, repair, fiber arts, and more.
cards.evidence_claim: The Billodue Makerspace is open to all Seattle University students and majors and offers activities including fiber arts, repair, laser cutting, and 3D printing.
cards.access_notes: Seattle University states the makerspace is open to all students and all majors; confirm equipment availability before visiting.

cards.title: Media Production Center
cards.subtitle: Lemieux Library & McGoldrick Learning Commons
cards.notes: Use the studio or editing-room equipment for a media assignment, then reserve enough time to export and review your final files.
cards.short_summary: A production-focused space with studio, editing, and screening-room resources.
cards.evidence_claim: The Media Production Center is available to all students and provides studio and editing-room equipment for video, photography, and audio production.
cards.access_notes: Available to all Seattle University students; review program offerings and equipment procedures before use.

cards.title: Veteran & Military-Connected Link
cards.subtitle: The Links by the MOSAIC Center
cards.notes: Use the tables, seating, and available study-room features for a focused session; check the current Link-hours graphic before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A MOSAIC Center community space with study-friendly furnishings and features.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University identifies the Veteran & Military-Connected Link as a Link space; Link spaces include tables, chairs, couches, and may have study rooms.
cards.access_notes: All students may check out Link spaces; all Links are closed weekends and holidays.

cards.title: Pride Link
cards.subtitle: The Links by the MOSAIC Center
cards.notes: Bring a reading or laptop task and use the shared tables or lounge seating; consult the current Link-hours graphic before arrival.
cards.short_summary: A MOSAIC Center community space that can support informal study sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University lists Pride Link among its Link spaces, which are equipped with tables, chairs, couches, and additional features that can include study rooms.
cards.access_notes: All students may check out Link spaces; all Links are closed weekends and holidays.

cards.title: Commuter & Transfer Link
cards.subtitle: The Links by the MOSAIC Center
cards.notes: Use this Link for a between-classes work block, taking advantage of its seating and study-oriented features; verify hours first.
cards.short_summary: A campus community space with tables, couches, and potential study-room access.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University identifies the Commuter & Transfer Link as a Link space; every Link space has tables, chairs, couches, and additional features such as study rooms.
cards.access_notes: All students may check out Link spaces; all Links are closed weekends and holidays.

cards.title: Graduate Student & Adult Learner Link
cards.subtitle: The Links by the MOSAIC Center
cards.notes: Choose a table or couch for independent work, and ask the MOSAIC Center about the Link’s specific study-room or shared-space setup.
cards.short_summary: A Link space supporting a campus learning community with flexible seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University lists the Graduate Student & Adult Learner Link among its Link spaces, which have tables, chairs, couches, and other features including study rooms.
cards.access_notes: All students may check out Link spaces; all Links are closed weekends and holidays.

cards.title: Intercultural Link
cards.subtitle: The Links by the MOSAIC Center
cards.notes: Settle in with course reading at a table or couch and check with staff about any study-room use or scheduled community programming.
cards.short_summary: A MOSAIC Center Link space with flexible, community-oriented study furnishings.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University identifies the Intercultural Link as a Link space; Link spaces are equipped with tables, chairs, couches, and additional features including study rooms.
cards.access_notes: All students may check out Link spaces; all Links are closed weekends and holidays.

cards.title: First-Gen Link
cards.subtitle: The Links by the MOSAIC Center
cards.notes: Use the shared seating for a low-key work session and check the current hours image before visiting, especially near holidays.
cards.short_summary: A campus Link space with tables, couches, and community-support resources.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University lists First-Gen Link as one of its Link spaces; each Link has tables, chairs, couches, and may include study rooms.
cards.access_notes: All students may check out Link spaces; all Links are closed weekends and holidays.

cards.entity_name: Seattle University Law Library Fourth Floor
cards.title: Seattle University Law Library Fourth Floor
cards.subtitle: Sullivan Hall
cards.notes: Choose this floor when silence matters, keep phones quiet, and use the library’s individual-study setting for concentrated reading or outlining.
cards.short_summary: A designated silent floor in the law library’s four-floor Sullivan Hall location.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University School of Law designates the Law Library’s fourth floor as a silent floor and states that carrels are available throughout the library.
cards.access_notes: Follow Law Library noise policies; carrels may not be held exclusively, and they are law-student-only during exam periods.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Named public destinations along the Broadway, First Hill, Pike-Pine, and Yesler corridors near Seattle University.

cards.title: See art at the Frye
cards.subtitle: Terry Avenue corridor, First Hill
cards.notes: Walk to 704 Terry Avenue and use the museum’s free admission to spend time with the exhibitions before continuing along First Hill.
cards.short_summary: A free art museum on Terry Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: The Frye Art Museum is at 704 Terry Avenue and states that admission is always free.
cards.access_notes: Museum and store hours listed: Wednesday–Sunday 11 a.m.–5 p.m.; Thursday until 8 p.m.

cards.title: Visit St. James Cathedral
cards.subtitle: 9th Avenue corridor, First Hill
cards.notes: Use the cathedral’s directions page to locate the building at 804 9th Avenue and check its current worship or visitor information before going.
cards.short_summary: A landmark cathedral on the First Hill side of 9th Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: St. James Cathedral lists its address as 804 9th Ave., Seattle, WA 98104.
cards.access_notes: Consult the cathedral’s current schedule before a visit.

cards.title: Pause at First Hill Park
cards.subtitle: University Street corridor, First Hill
cards.notes: Stop at 1201 University Street to see the custom bronze chair, ottoman, and bear-cub sculpture, then use the seating and lawn for a short break.
cards.short_summary: A compact city park with a distinctive bronze sculpture.
cards.evidence_claim: First Hill Park is at 1201 University Street and features a custom bronze sculpture of an Edwardian chair, ottoman, and two bear cubs.
cards.access_notes: City-listed park hours are 4 a.m.–11:30 p.m.

cards.title: Walk the park above I-5
cards.subtitle: Seneca Street corridor, First Hill
cards.notes: Enter at 700 Seneca Street and follow the paths through the landscaped park, which connects the First Hill edge with downtown over the freeway.
cards.short_summary: A 1976 park landscape built above Interstate 5.
cards.evidence_claim: Freeway Park is at 700 Seneca Street; the City says it was built atop a freeway and is bounded by Union, Spring, 6th, and 9th avenues.
cards.access_notes: City-listed park hours are 6 a.m.–10 p.m.; construction work may affect features.

cards.title: Use the Capitol Hill Branch
cards.subtitle: Harvard Avenue corridor, Capitol Hill
cards.notes: Head to 425 Harvard Avenue E. for public computers, Wi-Fi, printing, study rooms, and the branch’s LGBTQ+ collection during open library hours.
cards.short_summary: A public library branch with study and technology amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: The Capitol Hill Branch is at 425 Harvard Ave. E. and lists study rooms, public computers, Wi-Fi, and print/copy/scan among its amenities.
cards.source_title: Capitol Hill Branch | The Seattle Public Library
cards.access_notes: The library lists daily open hours and a 24/7 book return; verify schedule changes before traveling.

cards.title: Take the park loop
cards.subtitle: 11th Avenue corridor, Capitol Hill
cards.notes: Start at 1635 11th Avenue and use the city’s listed paths, reflecting pool, promenade, lawn, and oversized chess boards for an outdoor reset.
cards.short_summary: A city park with paths, water features, lawn, and chess boards.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal Anderson Park is at 1635 11th Ave. and includes promenade paths, a reflecting pool, athletic field, and oversized chess boards.
cards.access_notes: City-listed park hours are 4 a.m.–11:30 p.m.

cards.title: Find Seattle Central on Broadway
cards.subtitle: Broadway corridor, Capitol Hill
cards.notes: Walk to the main brick Broadway–Edison Building at 1701 Broadway; check building hours and only enter areas open to the public or scheduled visitors.
cards.short_summary: Seattle Central College’s main Broadway building.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle Central College identifies the Broadway–Edison Building at 1701 Broadway as its main brick building.
cards.source_title: Directions, Maps & Parking Info | Seattle Central College
cards.access_notes: The college posts building hours separately; access can be limited outside them.

cards.entity_name: Broadway & Marion First Hill Streetcar Stop
cards.title: Board the First Hill Streetcar
cards.subtitle: Broadway corridor at Marion Street
cards.notes: Use the Broadway & Marion stop as the First Hill connection point; confirm fare and service notices with Seattle Streetcar before boarding.
cards.short_summary: A named First Hill Streetcar stop on Broadway.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle’s First Hill Streetcar stop list includes Broadway & Marion in First Hill.
cards.source_title: First Hill Line | Seattle Department of Transportation
cards.access_notes: The City lists service through 10:30 p.m. Monday–Saturday and 8 p.m. Sunday/holidays; verify service alerts and fares.

cards.title: Climb the Horiuchi Park steps
cards.subtitle: Boren Avenue corridor, First Hill
cards.notes: Find the small staircase park at 156 Boren Avenue and take in the community garden and view before continuing between First Hill and Yesler.
cards.short_summary: A stair-step pocket park named for artist C. Paul Horiuchi.
cards.evidence_claim: Horiuchi Park is at 156 Boren Ave., is named for artist C. Paul Horiuchi, and is described by the City as a small staircase with a community garden.
cards.access_notes: City-listed park hours are 4 a.m.–11:30 p.m.

cards.title: Explore Yesler Terrace Park
cards.subtitle: Yesler Way corridor, Yesler Terrace
cards.notes: Visit the two-acre park at 917 E Yesler Way to use its plaza and walk past the sculptural installations; seasonal water features may vary.
cards.short_summary: A two-acre park with plaza, art installations, play, and sport amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: Yesler Terrace Park is at 917 E Yesler Way and includes a plaza, sculptural installations, playground, basketball court, and soccer spot.
cards.access_notes: City-listed park hours are 4 a.m.–11:30 p.m.; seasonal spraypark operations are subject to conditions.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Seattle University rituals and recurring events, from first-year welcome markers to spring community celebrations.

cards.title: Ring The Chapel Bell
cards.subtitle: New-student orientation tradition
cards.notes: During orientation, add this bell-ringing stop to your first-week plans and photograph the moment with your entering class.
cards.short_summary: A first-year marker that ceremonially begins a student’s time at Seattle U.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University identifies ringing the Chapel Bell during Orientation as an annual tradition for new students.
cards.access_notes: Presented as part of new-student Orientation; check Orientation programming for timing.

cards.title: Sign Your Entering Class Banner
cards.subtitle: New-student orientation tradition
cards.notes: Find the entering-class banner during orientation, sign your name clearly, and save a photo before moving on to other welcome events.
cards.short_summary: New students write their names into Seattle U history on their class banner.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University lists signing an entering class banner as a tradition for new students.
cards.access_notes: Offered through Orientation activities; confirm the current schedule with Orientation Programs.

cards.entity_name: Hawks Up At Your Class Photo
cards.title: Hawks Up At Your Class Photo
cards.subtitle: Entering-class photo ritual
cards.notes: Join the entering-class photo during orientation and use the linked-thumbs Hawks Up hand sign when the photographer calls for it.
cards.short_summary: The first class portrait pairs a Seattle U welcome photo with the Redhawk hand sign.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University lists Hawks Up at the class photo as a new-student tradition and publishes instructions for the gesture.
cards.access_notes: Class-photo timing is part of Orientation programming; follow staff directions onsite.

cards.title: Winter Ball
cards.subtitle: SEAC annual dance
cards.notes: Watch ConnectSU and SEAC announcements for the venue and dress guidance, then plan a group photo around the featured cultural setting.
cards.short_summary: A Student Events and Activities Council annual dance held at Seattle cultural venues.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University describes Winter Ball as a fun annual SU dance run by the Student Events and Activities Council.
cards.access_notes: Venue and event details vary by year; check ConnectSU or SEAC announcements.

cards.title: New Student Convocation
cards.subtitle: Fall-quarter academic ceremony
cards.notes: Put this opening ceremony on your Fall Welcome calendar and listen for the president, provost, and student-body president remarks.
cards.short_summary: Seattle U’s first academic ceremony formally marks the beginning of a new student’s journey.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University calls New Student Convocation an important rite of passage and the first SU academic ceremony for new students.
cards.access_notes: Scheduled during Fall Welcome; consult the current Welcome Events schedule.

cards.title: Mass of the Holy Spirit
cards.subtitle: Annual fall-quarter observance
cards.notes: If this observance fits your interests, check Campus Ministry’s fall schedule and attend at Immaculate Conception Church with the campus community.
cards.short_summary: A fall-quarter blessing for the new academic year, rooted in Catholic university practice.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University holds an annual Mass of the Holy Spirit at Immaculate Conception Church to seek blessings on the academic year.
cards.access_notes: Annual fall-quarter event; participation is open across religious, secular, and spiritual identities.

cards.title: New Student Retreat
cards.subtitle: Campus Ministry fall-quarter tradition
cards.notes: Apply through Campus Ministry early in fall if you want a small-group setting to reflect, meet peers, and begin the quarter together.
cards.short_summary: A fall retreat specifically designed to help first-year and transfer students build community.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University describes New Student Retreat as a fall-quarter Seattle U tradition for first-year and transfer undergraduates.
cards.access_notes: Offered by Campus Ministry each fall quarter; registration details are announced by Campus Ministry.

cards.title: Christmas Tree Lighting
cards.subtitle: Annual campus holiday gathering
cards.notes: Arrive for Student Center activities, then head outside for the lighting, chapel choir carols, and Redhawk mascot appearance.
cards.short_summary: Seattle U’s annual seasonal gathering combines indoor festivities with an outdoor tree-lighting ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University describes an annual Christmas Tree Lighting with Student Center festivities, chapel choir carols, and Rudy the Redhawk.
cards.access_notes: Annual seasonal program; verify the current date and activity details through student-event listings.

cards.title: International Dinner
cards.subtitle: International Student Center winter-quarter event
cards.notes: Look for winter-quarter registration details and come ready to watch cultural performances while learning from student organizers and community partners.
cards.short_summary: A student-organized dinner and performance program connecting campus cultures with the Seattle community.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University calls International Dinner a historic annual winter-quarter event, entirely student-organized, with food and cultural performances.
cards.access_notes: Hosted every winter quarter by the International Student Center; confirm the current event listing.

cards.title: Quadstock
cards.subtitle: SEAC annual music festival
cards.notes: Check SEAC’s spring announcements for the lineup and event rules, then plan to spend the day at this campus music-festival tradition.
cards.short_summary: An all-day annual music festival organized by the Student Events and Activities Council.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University describes Quadstock as SEAC’s annual, all-day music festival event.
cards.access_notes: Annual spring-quarter event; lineup, schedule, and access details change each year.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Seattle University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure first-weekend loop through Seattle U’s First Hill campus, ending with a nearby free art stop. Confirm event and facility access before participating.

cards.title: Start by mapping your bearings
cards.subtitle: Self-guided campus tour • First Hill
cards.notes: Register for the self-guided option, then begin outside the Chapel of St. Ignatius and use the tour stops to orient yourself before making plans.
cards.short_summary: A structured first look at the campus with a clearly identified starting point.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University’s self-guided tour begins outside the Chapel of St. Ignatius and lets visitors explore campus independently.
cards.access_notes: Registration is required for this self-guided-tour option; follow the confirmation instructions.

cards.title: Pause at the Chapel of St. Ignatius
cards.subtitle: Campus chapel • First Hill
cards.notes: Take a quiet look at the colored-light interior during open visiting hours, or attend a listed liturgy if that fits your own interests and schedule.
cards.short_summary: A campus landmark designed by Steven Holl, with visitor and liturgy information posted by Seattle U.
cards.evidence_claim: The Chapel of St. Ignatius is Seattle University’s main chapel; its architecture uses colored light and it is open for visiting Monday through Friday.
cards.source_title: Architecture of the Chapel of St. Ignatius
cards.access_notes: The chapel lists visiting hours of 8 a.m.–5 p.m. Monday–Friday; it is closed Saturdays except for special events and opens around Sunday Masses.

cards.title: Meet up on The Green
cards.subtitle: Campus green space • First Hill
cards.notes: Use this named campus stop as an easy daylight meeting point, then consult the campus map together to choose your next destination without rushing.
cards.short_summary: A named green-space landmark on Seattle U’s First Hill campus map.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University’s official First Hill campus map identifies The Green as a campus destination.
cards.access_notes: Use the official interactive map for current location and route details.

cards.entity_name: Lemieux Library and McGoldrick Learning Commons
cards.title: Find your library landing spot
cards.subtitle: Lemieux Library • First Hill
cards.notes: Walk through the library and learning commons, locate the service points you may need later, and save the building on your map for an easy return.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed library and learning-commons destination at the center of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University’s campus map identifies Lemieux Library and McGoldrick Learning Commons as a campus destination.
cards.access_notes: Some library spaces may require a Seattle University ID after hours; check library notices before visiting.

cards.title: Locate the Writing Center early
cards.subtitle: Second floor, Lemieux Library
cards.notes: Stop by the second floor of Lemieux to note the Writing Center’s location, then book a session when you have a draft, assignment, or idea to develop.
cards.short_summary: A student writing-support service located inside Lemieux Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University’s Writing Center is on the second floor of Lemieux Library and offers hour-long writing sessions.
cards.access_notes: The posted hours are Monday–Thursday 9 a.m.–8 p.m., Friday 9 a.m.–3 p.m., and Saturday 10 a.m.–1 p.m.; Sunday is closed.

cards.entity_name: Student Center and LeRoux Conference Center
cards.title: Get familiar with the Student Center
cards.subtitle: Student Center • First Hill
cards.notes: Use the campus map to find the Student Center and LeRoux Conference Center, then check current listings there for student-facing events and services.
cards.short_summary: A named campus destination that appears on Seattle U’s official map.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University’s official campus map identifies the Student Center and LeRoux Conference Center.
cards.access_notes: Consult current building postings or university event listings for open activities and access.

cards.entity_name: Redhawk Center and Eisiminger Fitness Center
cards.title: Scope out UREC
cards.subtitle: 14th and Cherry • South Campus
cards.notes: Walk over to the Redhawk Center and Eisiminger Fitness Center, identify the entrance, and check UREC’s current facility rules before planning a workout or recreation visit.
cards.short_summary: Seattle U’s recreation facilities are located at 14th Avenue and Cherry Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University identifies the Redhawk Center and Eisiminger Fitness Center as UREC facilities located on 14th and Cherry.
cards.access_notes: Facility access and participation are subject to current UREC policies; verify before entering or working out.

cards.title: Walk by Seattle University Park
cards.subtitle: Athletics field • South Campus
cards.notes: Pass the field on a daylight campus walk and check the athletics or recreation schedule before assuming the turf is available for informal use.
cards.short_summary: A synthetic-turf campus field used for varsity athletics, UREC, and club sports.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University Park is a synthetic-turf field that accommodates varsity athletics, UREC, and club sports.
cards.source_title: Seattle University Grounds, Waste Management and Pest Control
cards.access_notes: Field use can be scheduled; view from public campus routes and confirm availability before any activity.

cards.title: Spot Logan Field on the south side
cards.subtitle: Varsity softball field • South Campus
cards.notes: Add Logan Field to your south-campus loop, then look for posted activity rather than entering a practice or competition area without permission.
cards.short_summary: A Seattle U field used year-round for softball training, practices, and competition.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University states that Logan Field Varsity Softball accommodates training, practices, and competition play year-round.
cards.source_title: Seattle University Grounds, Waste Management and Pest Control
cards.access_notes: This is an athletics facility; observe posted restrictions and scheduled activities.

cards.title: End the campus loop at Championship Field
cards.subtitle: Soccer field • South Campus
cards.notes: Find the field from the campus walk, then watch for a publicly listed game or event instead of relying on an assumed open-field schedule.
cards.short_summary: Seattle U’s natural-turf field and home venue for its soccer teams.
cards.evidence_claim: Championship Field is a Seattle University sports field that accommodates training, practices, and competition; Seattle U identifies it as home to its soccer teams.
cards.source_title: Championship Field Ready for Its Closeup
cards.access_notes: Access depends on scheduled athletics and events; use Seattle U’s event listing for current public events.
